subsystems.name: Quantum processing unit
subsystems.role: the hardware that stores and manipulates quantum bits.

subsystems.name: Quantum error correction and mitigation
subsystems.role: keeps computations reliable despite noise and decoherence.

subsystems.name: Quantum algorithm layer
subsystems.role: provides quantum routines for biological problems.

subsystems.name: Biological data encoding
subsystems.role: maps DNA, RNA and protein data onto quantum states.

subsystems.name: Hybrid classical–quantum workflow
subsystems.role: orchestrates quantum subroutines inside conventional bioinformatics pipelines.

subsystems.name: Application layer
subsystems.role: targets specific tasks in genomics and drug discovery.

buildSteps.title: Select a qubit platform
buildSteps.detail: Choose superconducting, trapped-ion, photonic or neutral-atom hardware based on required qubit count, connectivity and coherence time.

buildSteps.title: Design quantum algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Develop or adapt quantum routines — for example dynamic-programming circuits for sequence alignment or variational eigensolvers for molecular energies.

buildSteps.title: Encode biological data
buildSteps.detail: Convert DNA sequences, protein conformations or molecular Hamiltonians into quantum states using amplitude, angle or Hamiltonian encoding.

buildSteps.title: Implement error handling
buildSteps.detail: Add error-correcting codes or mitigation techniques so that noisy hardware returns meaningful results.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with classical tools
buildSteps.detail: Build a hybrid pipeline where a classical computer prepares inputs, calls the quantum processor and interprets outputs against existing bioinformatics databases.

buildSteps.title: Validate on small cases
buildSteps.detail: Run benchmarks on problems small enough for classical simulation, checking that quantum results match known biological answers.

buildSteps.title: Scale and demonstrate advantage
buildSteps.detail: Extend to larger genomes or drug-like molecules where a quantum machine outperforms the best classical method in speed or accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in discovery workflows
buildSteps.detail: Embed the validated quantum step into pharmaceutical R&D or clinical genomics pipelines, with regulatory and reproducibility checks.

prerequisites.why: most bioinformatics problems need thousands of logical qubits, far beyond today's noisy devices.
small proofs-of-concept exist for sequence alignment and molecular simulation, but none has shown practical advantage.
loading large genomic datasets into a quantum computer is itself a bottleneck.
genome databases, alignment tools and protein-structure archives are needed to frame and verify quantum results.
basic codes have been demonstrated, but not at the scale required for long biological computations.

pathway.milestone: noisy small-scale experiments on tens of qubits, mostly simulating tiny molecules or toy alignment problems
pathway.unlocks: understanding which biological tasks might benefit from quantum speed-up.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant devices with hundreds of logical qubits running hybrid quantum-classical bioinformatics workflows
pathway.unlocks: credible benchmarks against classical algorithms on real genomic or drug-discovery data.

pathway.milestone: first demonstrated quantum advantage on a narrow, well-defined bioinformatics task
pathway.unlocks: investment and standardisation for quantum-enhanced drug discovery.

pathway.milestone: routine integration into pharmaceutical pipelines and clinical genomics
pathway.unlocks: faster design of new medicines and more accurate personalised treatments.
